author: Jason Redman
quotes: Adversity becomes permanent only when you build your identity around the impact point.
Move away from the place where failure pinned you.
A crisis is not the time to begin practicing responsibility.
The first step after disaster may be choosing not to remain psychologically trapped there.
Your wounds can become evidence of survival without becoming your entire identity.
Leadership is most visible when the original plan has been destroyed.
A strong team prepares for disruption rather than assuming perfect conditions.
You cannot control the ambush, but you can influence the next movement.
The path forward begins by accurately identifying where you are.
Do not let shame keep you stationary after the mistake.
Recovery requires movement before it offers confidence.
The response to adversity often matters longer than the adversity itself.
Preparation creates options when chaos removes comfortable choices.
A damaged plan does not mean the mission has lost all meaning.
Your darkest moment may become a rallying point rather than a grave.
Leadership includes admitting when your own decisions helped create the problem.
Stop replaying the impact long enough to identify the exit.
Resilience is not denial; it is deliberate movement through reality.
The people around you need your honesty more than your performance of invulnerability.
A setback becomes a position, and positions can be changed.
Courage may look like asking for help before the situation deteriorates further.
You can honor what was lost without surrendering everything that remains.
The next action should move you toward safety, clarity, or renewed purpose.
Do not build a permanent camp at the site of a temporary defeat.
Assess the damage, accept responsibility, and begin moving again.
